policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 6:5 ends at 'supposing that godliness is a way of gain.' with no rendering of the RP addition 'Ἀφίστασο ἀπὸ τῶν τοιούτων' ('from such withdraw thyself'), and no note supplies it; the absent imperative clause distinguishes the base reading.

ASV 6:7 reads 'for we brought nothing into the world, for neither can we carry anything out' with nothing answering to RP's δῆλον ('it is manifest/certain that'); the missing predicate distinguishes bare ὅτι.

The variant is only the presence of the Greek article before θεοῦ; ASV 'O man of God' renders anarthrous and articular genitive identically, and the sole note on the verse is classed alternative_rendering, so nothing in the English distinguishes the readings. Base fallback carries the projection.

ASV renders the final virtue simply 'meekness', which serves πραϋπαθίαν and πρᾳότητα alike; the verse's 'Or, stedfastness' note is classed alternative_rendering and attaches to the English of 'patience', so it cannot decide a reading.

ASV 'who giveth life to all things' is an equally natural rendering of ζῳογονοῦντος and ζωοποιοῦντος; the margin 'Or, preserveth all things alive' is classed alternative_rendering and by policy speaks to English wording rather than to the Greek reading, so the unit stays underdetermined.

ASV 'have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches' renders ἐπί and ἐν τῷ alike as 'on'; the verse's only note ('Or, age') is alternative_rendering and bears on 'this present world', not on this preposition.
ASV 6:17 reads 'but on God, who giveth us richly all things' with no 'living' answering to RP's added τῷ ζῶντι; the absent adjective distinguishes the base reading.
ASV 'lay hold on the life which is life indeed' renders ὄντως ('indeed'); RP's αἰωνίου would give 'eternal life', which the ASV does not read here.
ASV closes 'Grace be with you.' — plural 'you', where ASV renders a singular σοῦ as 'thee' — and prints no 'Amen' for RP's Ἀμήν; both features distinguish μεθ᾽ ὑμῶν.
